specification.problem: Exactly identify an unknown multilinear polynomial f over F_2 in n=3 variables with degree at most 2 (7 coefficients: c_0, c_1..c_3, c_12, c_13, c_23) using a naive derivative-based Bernstein-Vazirani scheme. The coefficients are hard-coded into the oracle for functional simulation only, and no query-complexity claim is made.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Only the tiny instance n=3, d=2, q=2, with a naive full-identification circuit that recovers all 7 coefficients exactly. It runs three controlled-derivative BV blocks, one per direction e_i, plus one f(0) block. Each block uses its own register. This costs 7 controlled-oracle calls, versus 7 classical monomials, so it is NOT the paper's O(n^(d-1)) exact algorithm. Out of scope: general q and d, the optimal query construction and orthogonality argument, the lower bound, and any black-box query-count certification.

symbols.meaning: coefficient of monomial prod_{i in S} x_i
linear part of D_i f as a bit vector, with l^{(i)}_j=c_{ij} for j!=i and l^{(i)}_i=0

equations.label: Multilinear polynomial
equations.description: Parametrization of the unknown polynomial, with 7 coefficients for n=3, d=2.
equations.abstract_quote: identify an unknown multilinear polynomial of degree d in n variables over a finite field Fq
equations.justification: The abstract names multilinear polynomials of degree d. The explicit sum form is a standard definition, specialized to q=2.

equations.label: Phase oracle and its controlled version
equations.description: The oracle is diagonal. Each monomial is compiled into Z, CZ or CCZ on x, and the controlled version adds one control qubit b (CZ, CCZ, CCCZ).
equations.justification: Explicit classical coefficients are compiled into gates for functional simulation. This is not an opaque oracle.

equations.label: Derivative of a multilinear polynomial
equations.description: For multilinear f with deg<=2 the derivative in direction e_i is affine and independent of x_i. Its constant term is c_i and its linear part is l^{(i)}.
equations.justification: Direct expansion over F_2 with x_i^2=x_i. It is used as a candidate degree-reduction step and is not claimed to be the paper's method.
assumptions: multilinear, so each variable appears with exponent at most 1

equations.label: Controlled-derivative BV block
equations.description: The ancilla a_i is in |+> and the x^{(i)} register is uniform. The controlled phase is (-1)^{b D_if(x)}, with X_i acting on qubit i of x^{(i)}, and it uses two controlled-O_f calls. The H layers then give the affine function's constant c_i on a_i and its linear part on x^{(i)}. Phase kickback onto b makes the constant exactly recoverable, with no global-phase loss.
equations.justification: Exact identity from eq_2 and eq_3. The phase is (-1)^{b(c_i+l.x)}. H on x gives |l> with sign (-1)^{b c_i}, and H on b gives |c_i>.
assumptions: Derivative oracle built from two controlled-O_f calls

equations.label: Constant term block
equations.description: The z register stays in |000>, so the controlled phase is (-1)^{b f(0)}=(-1)^{b c_0}. H on a_0 then reads out c_0.
equations.justification: f(0)=c_0 by eq_1. The controlled oracle turns the global sign into a relative phase.
assumptions: The z register is not Hadamarded

registers.name: x1
registers.role: BV register for the e_1 derivative block. Qubit j is x_j, with qubit 0 least significant. Output is l^{(1)}=(0,c_12,c_13).

registers.name: x2
registers.role: BV register for the e_2 derivative block. Output is l^{(2)}=(c_12,0,c_23).

registers.name: x3
registers.role: BV register for the e_3 derivative block. Output is l^{(3)}=(c_13,c_23,0).

registers.name: a1
registers.role: Control/kickback ancilla for block 1. Output is c_1.

registers.name: a2
registers.role: Control/kickback ancilla for block 2. Output is c_2.

registers.name: a3
registers.role: Control/kickback ancilla for block 3. Output is c_3.

registers.name: a0
registers.role: Ancilla for the constant block. Output is c_0 (the oracle acts on a fixed |000> register, so 3 extra qubits are needed unless one reuses the x registers).

registers.name: z
registers.role: Fixed |000> register on which the controlled oracle is evaluated for the c_0 block

specification.initial_state: All qubits in |0>; total 16 qubits (x1,x2,x3: 9; a1,a2,a3,a0: 4; z: 3).

steps.description: Input preparation: apply H to every qubit of x1,x2,x3 and to a0,a1,a2,a3. Leave z in |000>. The coefficients c_S are classical build parameters compiled into the oracle.
For each i in {1,2,3}: apply C-O_f (control a_i, target x_i), then X on qubit i of x_i, then C-O_f again, then X on qubit i of x_i. This implements the controlled derivative phase.
Constant block: apply C-O_f with control a0 and target z (in |000>).
Apply H to all qubits of x1,x2,x3 and to a0,a1,a2,a3. The final state is a computational basis state encoding all coefficients.

specification.measurement: Output decoding: the circuit is measurement-free, so read the computational-basis state of the final simulated state. Read c_0 from a0, c_i from a_i, and c_ij from x_i qubit j (j!=i). The c_ij are redundantly available from x_i and x_j and should agree.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Fixed classical map: c_0=a0, c_i=a_i, c_12=x1[2] (equal to x2[1]), c_13=x1[3], c_23=x2[3], with 1-indexed qubit positions inside each x register. Check redundancy consistency x_i[j]=x_j[i].
assumptions: Tiny instance n=3, d=2, q=2 chosen by me
Naive derivative-BV scheme using 7 controlled-oracle calls, no query-efficiency claim
The oracle only accepts monomials with |S|<=2
Qubit j of each x register holds x_j, with qubit 0 as x_1
missing_information: The paper's actual exact O(n^(d-1)) query algorithm and its state-orthogonality construction
